headline.caveat: ~$20B cash for a non-exclusive license to Groq's inference-chip technology plus senior talent — a technology/IP license, not a model license; not structured as an acquisition

nature_md: NVIDIA's largest deal ever: ~$20B in cash for a **non-exclusive license** to Groq's LPU inference technology, with founder-CEO Jonathan Ross and several senior executives joining NVIDIA — a 'not-acqui-hire' announced in late December 2025. Groq itself was not acquired: GroqCloud continues independently under new leadership and raised $650M in June 2026 to re-staff (confirmed by Groq). Senators Warren and Blumenthal wrote to Jensen Huang in March 2026 questioning whether the structure was designed to evade Hart-Scott-Rodino merger review while eliminating an inference-chip competitor. Recorded under `model_license` as the closest schema type for a technology-licensing transaction.

accounting.payer_treatment_md: For NVIDIA, capitalized as acquired intangibles (licensed IP) amortized over useful life, plus compensation expense for hired talent — likely far below the $20B headline in annual P&L terms. No entity consolidation since no control was acquired — the feature the senators flagged.
accounting.payee_treatment_md: For Groq, transformational one-time licensing proceeds (revenue or gain, depending on structure) that dwarf its ~$6.9B prior valuation; the company retained the right to keep using its own technology and continues selling inference via GroqCloud.

both_sides_md: **Bear (Warren/Blumenthal + antitrust critics):** $20B for a license-plus-leadership from your most credible inference competitor is a de facto acquisition engineered around merger review — market consolidation without regulator sign-off. **Bull:** the license is non-exclusive, Groq survives as an independent competitor with fresh capital, and NVIDIA paying for inference IP shows genuine technology value rather than a shutdown (deal terms per press; Groq's June 2026 re-raise as evidence of continued independence).

events.title: Senators Warren and Blumenthal query NVIDIA's $20B Groq deal on antitrust grounds
